summary: Completed backend-only, read-only offline diagnosis using source review plus dependency-free pytest simulations. Confirmed multiple code-level defects matching the incident hypotheses; no live endpoints/DB/WhatsApp/Stripe were called.

critical.issue: Activation hardcodes activated=true and welcome_sent=true even when per-parent sends fail; result payload can include failed statuses while state is marked activated.
No activation-day guard for overdue slots; scheduler sends all past same-day slots at once when first activated/recovered.
Absolute daily cap uses unfiltered count(*) from message_logs; failed rows consume cap and can block valid sends.
Failure retry budget is category-level (not slot-level). Failures for one slot/category can block later distinct slots same day.
Medicine dedup key uses category+slot_time (no medicine identity), so two medicines at same time collapse and second medicine can be skipped.
Vacation bypass: care-watch and reengagement paths do not check vacation_start/vacation_end, so warning/nudge flows can run during pause period.

minor.issue: Parent first warning at 2pm uses plain send_whatsapp despite dedicated send_first_warning_to_parent template helper existing.
Signup welcome is currently a no-op (returns skipped:gated until first parent added).
Inbound from non-parent number is ignored early (returns ignored=true).

integration_issues.issue: Frontend persists legacy /schedules only; no code bridge found to granular parent_checkins/parent_health_reminders/parent_routines/medicines APIs used by scheduler.
Dashboard pause toggles legacy schedules.active, but scheduler reads granular tables directly and does not consult schedules.active.

action_items: Fix activation success semantics: derive activated/welcome_sent from actual send outcomes and persist partial failures explicitly.
Add activation-day and catch-up throttling strategy for overdue slots.
Change daily cap query to count only sent/simulated (or dedicated billable/delivered statuses).
Track retry counters per category+slot (and medicine_id where applicable), not only category.
Include medicine_id (or unique reminder key) in dedup criteria for medicine sends.
Enforce vacation guard in reengagement and care-watch flows.
Use template helper for parent first warning and keep fallback only when template unavailable.
Implement explicit bridge/migration path between legacy /schedules UI and granular schedule tables (or retire legacy path fully).
Resolve pre-existing duplicate definitions/imports: duplicate CHECKIN_CATEGORIES shadowing, duplicate delete_routine route, monthly_report duplicate helpers/imports and bare except blocks.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py imports CHECKIN_CATEGORIES from templates_data and later redefines CHECKIN_CATEGORIES locally (shadowing risk).
server.py contains duplicate delete_routine endpoint definitions for the same route signature.
monthly_report.py has duplicated import/helper block and 4 bare except statements (baseline lint/safety concern).
Pricing inconsistency confirmed in code: Nitya INR yearly=950 vs monthly=949.
payments.py checkout is always one-time Stripe mode=payment and currency=usd regardless currency presentation in pricing cards.

context_for_next_testing_agent: This iteration is diagnosis-only and static/offline by design. No live validation against production integrations was performed. Use this report to drive targeted fixes, then run isolated regression for scheduler/escalation activation semantics and finally controlled staging E2E with real WhatsApp template/session behavior.
rca of the issue: Core RCA is code-path mismatch: message delivery and escalation logic has split sources of truth (legacy schedules vs granular tables), broad dedup/retry keys, and unconditional success flags. This explains symptoms like missing child updates, burst/flood then stop, and inconsistent warning behavior. Evidence is from exact source lines and dependency-free offline simulations; not from live production replay.
